findings.element: Integration selector (Integration) sharing one matching-rule draft/saved state
findings.finding: The matching-rule configurator keeps a single saved/draft rule object that isn't keyed by the selected integration, so switching the Integration selector between two different integrations shows (and would save) the same rule set as belonging to whichever one is currently picked.
findings.user_impact: An accountant setting up a custom rule for one integration and then switching to review another integration on the same client (or a different client) could unknowingly carry that rule over and save it against the wrong integration, causing payments there to be matched to the wrong invoices.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the saved/draft matching-rule state by integration id and reload the correct rule set whenever the Integration selector changes.

evidence.source: vocabulary.md Organizational Terms — "Organization ... has accounting company + integrations + subscription plan": each integration is a distinct entity, so matching-rule configuration must not bleed across integrations.

findings.element: "Update" button on the Invoices settings page (gspUpdate) — confirmation toast
findings.finding: Saving the book-affecting Invoices toggles (Apply payments, Cancel sync, Sync unpaid invoices, Sync zero invoices) confirms with an internal codename instead of a real product term.
findings.user_impact: A bookkeeper working across many client integrations gets no indication from the confirmation of what was actually changed, undermining confidence that a book-affecting settings change really saved.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the toast with a concrete confirmation naming the actual settings, e.g. "Invoice settings updated!", following the {Thing} {past participle}! pattern.

evidence.source: vocabulary.md Toast Patterns (Success: "{Thing} {past participle}!", e.g. "Settings updated!") — "GSP" is not in the UI Words canonical terms table and the toast is missing the required exclamation mark.

findings.element: "Apply payments to unpaid Invoice transactions" toggle vs. the overlay title "Apply payments to invoices in books"
findings.finding: The same rule is called "unpaid Invoice transactions" on the settings row (and its sub-copy "the matching unpaid Invoice transaction") but "invoices in books" one click away in the overlay it opens, mixing a synced transaction record with a ledger invoice for the same setting.
findings.user_impact: An accountant could believe the toggle governs which incoming platform transactions get synced rather than which invoice already posted in the books a payment is applied to, risking a misconfigured rule for the exact task this screen exists for.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one consistent term — "invoices in your books" — in both the settings-row label/description and the overlay title, reserving "transaction" for the payment/platform side.

evidence.quote: Apply payments to unpaid Invoice transactions
evidence.source: Domain scope: "Missing distinctions: flows that blur payment vs. invoice vs. transaction vs. payout"; vocabulary.md Books vs. Integration distinction (ledger inside the accounting company vs. the data source).

gaps: "Apply payments to unpaid Invoice transactions" master toggle: recon only recorded turning it off (which disables the Configure link); it was never switched back on with the configurator reopened, so whether a previously saved custom matching rule survives that off/on cycle intact is unknown.
